content:
Apple released the M6 chip today, which belongs to an entirely new chip generation and will also be used in the A20 Pro in the iPhone 18 Pro. Below is the performance improvement information for the iPhone 18 Pro revealed by the M6.

The M6 shows that the iPhone 18 Pro's A20 Pro will see substantial gains in performance and efficiency.

September is still a while away, but Apple today surprised everyone with the launch of two new products: the new Mac mini and Mac Studio. (Available for pre-order starting today: Mac mini, Mac Studio.)

The Mac mini is equipped with Apple's next-generation M6 chip, which belongs to the same chip family as the A20 Pro that will soon be used in the iPhone 18 Pro.

Here is the official introduction from Apple Newsroom:

The M6 adopts the most advanced 2-nanometer process technology, packing higher transistor density into a smaller chip to achieve a significant leap in performance and energy efficiency. The M6 also debuts a dual 16-core Neural Engine, with peak computing power up to twice that of the previous generation, enabling faster on-device AI workflows. ... The M6 features a brand-new 12-core CPU architecture—two more cores than the M5—comprising 2 super cores, 4 performance cores, and 6 efficiency cores. It delivers the world's fastest single-threaded performance, with multi-threaded performance up to 1.2 times faster than the M5.

The M6's final performance will be more powerful than the new A20 Pro chip in the iPhone 18 Pro. This is generally the case with Mac- and iPad-class M-series chips.

However, since both the M6 and the A20 Pro belong to the same chip family, the upgrades seen in the M6 are expected to appear on the A20 Pro as well.

Most notably, the A20 Pro will adopt the new 2-nanometer process highlighted by the M6, bringing a "significant leap in performance and energy efficiency."

We had previously speculated that the transition to the 2-nanometer process would bring larger-than-usual performance gains. The details of the M6 confirm this.

The CPU and GPU core counts of the A20 Pro may not be identical to those of the M6. The dual 16-core Neural Engine is also uncertain. But thanks to 2-nanometer technology, it should bring major improvements in the two areas Apple emphasized today: performance and efficiency.

What will the specific year-over-year gains look like? It's still hard to say for now. But when the iPhone 18 Pro is unveiled in a few weeks, performance and efficiency are expected to be the main upgrade highlights for the A20 Pro.
